title: Capital budget project classifications for 2024–2026
subtitle: Parkland funds transfer, Generation Park surplus lands, committee reappointments and a public meeting on 446 Albert Street.
overview: Council spent most of the day sorting 2024–2026 capital projects into routine and non-routine. Routine projects can start after budget adoption on February 12, 2024. Non-routine projects must return to Council for approval before money is spent. Most departments' projects were approved as routine, with several moved to non-routine, including some tied to staffing requests that Council will decide on next week. The transportation package, which moved one Columbia Street project to non-routine, passed {{vote:m28}}.

Council also moved $4,405,000 from the Northdale portion of the Parkland Dedication Reserve Fund to the general portion, so it can fund parkland needs across the city. It declared the Generation Park lands surplus and re-appointed three Kitchener residents to the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee.

In the evening, Council held an informal public meeting on a proposed 13-tower development at 446 Albert Street. No decision was made, and staff will report back later. The mayor also noted that the city is receiving $22 million from the federal Housing Accelerator Fund. The minutes report no outcome from the closed session.

decisions.detail: Council approved report CORP2024-002, which sets out the routine and non-routine classifications for the 2024–2026 capital budget ahead of budget adoption on February 12, 2024.
Council approved moving $4,405,000 from the Northdale portion to the general portion of the Parkland Dedication Reserve Fund to fund parkland needs citywide.
Council declared surplus the city-owned blocks on Registered Plan 58M-704 at Generation Park, and a by-law confirming this was later passed.
Council re-appointed three applicants to the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee for terms ending December 31, 2027, pending ratification by the partnering municipalities.
Council classified these projects as routine but moved capital ref #132, which is tied to a staffing request, to non-routine.
Council classified planning projects as routine but moved refs #620 and #623, the latter being future Northdale parks work, to non-routine so they return to Council before spending.
Council classified transportation projects as routine but moved ref #670 to non-routine so the separated cycling plans can be reviewed first, carried {{vote:m28}}.

debate: On the parkland transfer, one councillor asked about the history of the Northdale fund and the risks of not transferring. Staff said the 2024–2026 budget already counts on the transfer, so a refusal or deferral would mean removing parkland-funded projects. Staff said enough Northdale money would remain for local needs, and general parkland funds could still be spent there later.

On staffing-linked projects, councillors debated whether to make all eight non-routine at once. One councillor argued a low-cost project in an under-capacity team should stay routine. Staff said a single finance report after budget day could reclassify projects without each division writing its own report.

At the 446 Albert Street public meeting, residents objected to the proposed height and density, including the tallest tower near the Sugar Bush woodlot. They also raised cut-through traffic, dangerous corners, school-route safety, parking spillover and the cumulative effect of several nearby developments.

Other speakers supported the project because of the housing shortage, but asked for more two- and three-bedroom units. Councillors asked staff to look at expanding the traffic study area, daily traffic volumes, the school bus loading plan and possible impacts on Sugar Bush. They also asked about a second open house.

The applicant's team said the site is a contaminated brownfield near transit, with about a quarter of it set aside as publicly accessible open space. It also said affordable units would be spread through the site, and that geothermal heating was ruled out by the region.
